old: then drew up a polished table beside them
new: then drew up a clean table beside them
reason: Butler: "she drew a clean table beside them"; this hospitality formula is "a clean table" in every accepted Book (B01-P010, B04-P005, B07-P015, B10-P028, B15-P010), and "polished" is a detail Butler does not give.

old: By Zeus, Athena, and Apollo,
new: By father Zeus, Athena, and Apollo,
reason: Butler: "By father Jove, Minerva, and Apollo"; the draft drops "father", and accepted B04-P027 prints this same speech as "By father Zeus, Athena, and Apollo".

old: A doe might as well lay her newborn fawns in a lion’s den, then go off to graze in the forest or meadow.
new: A hind might as well lay her newborn young in the lair of a lion, and then go off to feed in the forest or in some grassy dell.
reason: Butler: "A hind might as well lay her new-born young in the lair of a lion, and then go off to feed in the forest or in some grassy dell"; the draft drops the "grassy dell" image, and accepted B04-P027 renders this repeated speech "A hind … new born young in the lair of a lion … or in some grassy hollow" (Butler's B04 word), so "doe"/"fawns"/"den" break the echo.

old: they’d have a quick death and a bitter wedding
new: they’d have short shrift and a sorry wedding
reason: Butler: "they would have a short shrift and a sorry wedding"; accepted B04-P027 keeps Butler's phrase in this same speech, so the repeat should echo it.

old: and I told him everything. Then he said,
new: and I told him the whole truth. At that he said,
reason: Butler: "I told him the whole truth, whereon he said"; GLOSSARY Book 4 row renders "whereon" as "at that" (the notes claim this repair but the draft prints "Then"), and "the whole truth" is flattened.

old: As he passed, he kicked Odysseus
new: At this, as he passed, he kicked Odysseus
reason: Butler: "On this, as he passed, he gave Ulysses a kick"; GLOSSARY's Book 4 row renders every Butler "On this" as "At this", and the comma here is Butler's own (it closes off "as he passed"), exactly as accepted B10-P044 prints "At this, many dead men’s ghosts" for Butler's "On this, many dead men’s ghosts"; dropping the connective loses that the kick answers his speech.

old: everyone who sees you will call you blessed
new: everyone who sees you will congratulate you
reason: Butler: "all who see you shall congratulate you"; accepted B15-P044 keeps "congratulate you" in this formula, and "call you blessed" adds a scriptural colouring Butler does not have.

old: leaned his spear against a post of the gallery
new: leaned his spear against a pillar of the gallery
reason: Butler: "a bearing-post of the cloister"; accepted Book 16 (previous Book, B16-P037 "one of the pillars supporting the roof of the gallery") and B01-P009, B08-P004/P041/P043 render Butler's bearing-post as "pillar"; the draft reverted live's "pillar" to a new term.

old: by one of the posts of the gallery
new: by one of the pillars of the gallery
reason: Butler: "by one of the bearing-posts of the cloister"; same reason as ¶2 (B16-P037 "one of the pillars supporting the roof of the gallery").

old: against a cypress-wood post
new: against a cypress-wood pillar
reason: Butler: "against a bearing-post of cypress-wood"; same reason as ¶2 (accepted Books render bearing-post "pillar").

old: I’d have liked you to stay here as a farmhand
new: I’d have liked you to stay here as a hand at the station
reason: Butler: "to stay here as a station hand"; accepted Book 16 keeps Eumaeus's "station" (B16-P008, P009 ×2, P014), and this Book keeps "station" for Melanthius's at ¶18, so "farm" makes one place two things.

old: leaving the farm in charge of the dogs
new: leaving the station in charge of the dogs
reason: Butler: "leaving the station in charge of the dogs"; same reason as ¶15.

old: picked up a stool that was lying near where the server sat
new: picked up a seat that was lying near where the carver sat
reason: Butler: "saw a seat lying near where the carver sat"; accepted B01-P010, B03-P007, B04-P005 keep "carver", and "stool" is not Butler's word here and blurs this seat with Antinous's footstool (¶40, ¶45).

old: There’s nothing wrong with eating when it’s mealtime.
new: Dinner is not a bad thing at dinnertime.
reason: Butler: "Dinner is not a bad thing, at dinner time"; Medon's joke is the deliberate repetition, which the draft loses.

old: I understand, and will do as you say.
new: I understand and will obey.
reason: Butler: "I understand and heed"; the notes correctly reject "be careful", but the previous accepted Book renders Butler's same formula (B16-P012 "I understand and heed you") as "I understand and will obey".

old: unless he were someone useful—a seer
new: unless he were someone who can do public service—a seer
reason: Butler: "unless it be one of those who can do public service as a seer"; "public service" is the point (such men serve the whole people), and "useful" drops it.

old: all the other things that make people prosperous and respected
new: all the other things people have who live well and are thought wealthy
reason: Butler: "all the other things which people have who live well and are accounted wealthy"; "respected" replaces being reckoned rich.

old: such a plague to plague us
new: such a pestilence to plague us
reason: Butler: "such a pestilence to plague us"; the notes' claim that Butler wrote "plague to plague" is wrong, and the draft invents the repetition.

old: that meant exactly this
new: that meant this
reason: Butler: "I saw an omen when I was on the ship which meant this"; "exactly" is an added intensifier (GLOSSARY Voice and form).

old: May Zeus destroy them before they harm us.
new: May Zeus bring them to a bad end before they do us harm.
reason: Butler: "May Jove bring them to a bad end before they do us a mischief"; the draft intensifies the wish, and the phrase echoes Odysseus's own "come to a bad end" at ¶46.

old: Eumaeus went back to the suitors, having explained everything
new: Eumaeus went back to the suitors, for he had explained everything
reason: Butler: "Eumaeus went back to the suitors, for he had explained everything"; the causal "for" becomes a participle.
